turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct. Why is there a zero next to Owen's name?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
I didn't come for thanks, Hale. A zero went in on November 3rd and nobody called me. Who decided that, and on what basis?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess, Hale. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for acting against a student. So what else do you have, or is that it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

Quite reliable. Fourteen detection tools were tested in 2023 and the finding was "neither accurate nor reliable." Your own procedure, 4.3, says software doesn't establish a concern by itself, so I'll ask again: what else do you have?
So I had to give him a zero.

"Had to." Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in. So you decided first and asked questions later. Did you speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
I hope you understand my position.

"I hope." Okay. My position is on the page in front of you, Hale: you didn't call me, you didn't answer whether Owen was heard, and the only thing you've given me is a score. Withdraw the zero, or tell me what else you have.
